directions.description: Replace single-negative BPR with multi-negative BPR-max, emphasizing difficult negatives. The authors provide the loss and score regularization in their [official implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/blob/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py), accompanying the [Top-k Gains paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03847). This is a hypothesis for validation, not a measured improvement here.
directions.implementation:
Common requirements for ALL four independent proposals: retain the supplied GRU backbone, shifted causal targets, all four categories and routing. Set DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; keep training seed 42, preprocessing seed 0, 200 batches/epoch and at most 200 epochs, respecting the host's SASREC_EPOCHS=200 default. Write only beneath the trial directory. Keep one selected checkpoint/category, with no averaging or score fusion. Preserve the host evaluator; any local validation must use fixed seed-42 users and unique negatives without advancing training RNG. Implement log2feats(sequence) as the causal GRU sequence output and reuse it in forward and encode. Implement predict_score(features, items) using the same item scoring operation as training. Retain item_emb. encode must gather the maximum nonpadding position, as supplied. Predictor generation must import the updated model class and reconstruct every architecture setting from checkpoint metadata.

For this proposal, retain baseline architecture and Adam(lr=1e-3). Extend sampled negative IDs from [B,T] to [B,T,K], initially K=64. Draw uniformly from 1..itemnum, rejecting each user's training interactions; never use validation labels for training sampling. Keep sample_batch's three-return interface and adjust the loss consumer for the additional negative dimension. Flatten only valid target positions before embedding/scoring; process them in chunks of 1024 to bound GPU memory.

Core loss on each chunk:
import torch.nn.functional as F
h = model.log2feats(seq)[pos.ne(0)]
y = pos[pos.ne(0)]
n = neg[pos.ne(0)]
s_pos = (h * model.item_emb(y)).sum(-1)
s_neg = torch.einsum('nd,nkd->nk', h, model.item_emb(n))
log_w = F.log_softmax(s_neg, dim=-1)
ranking = -torch.logsumexp(log_w + F.logsigmoid(s_pos[:, None] - s_neg), dim=-1)
regularizer = 0.1 * (log_w.exp() * s_neg.square()).sum(-1)
loss = (ranking + regularizer).mean()

Use linear logits consistently at inference. Aggregate chunk losses weighted by valid-position count, then take one optimizer step per batch. Store only the validation-selected checkpoint, not a combination of epochs.

directions.description: Test sampled multiclass cross-entropy instead of pairwise BPR. This alternative is supported by the authors' [official GRU4Rec code](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/blob/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py). Retain the recurrent architecture and tied item embeddings.
directions.implementation:
Apply the common requirements in direction 1. Begin independently from the corrected baseline, rather than combining independently trained models. Keep hidden size 128, one GRU layer, input dropout 0.1 and Adam(lr=1e-3). Replace the BPR objective with sampled cross-entropy using K=256 uniform negatives per valid training position. Sample IDs with replacement from 1..itemnum and reject the current positive; other training-history items remain eligible in this particular multiclass objective. Keep the original shifted positive targets. Preserve sample_batch's three-return interface, returning negatives shaped [B,T,K].

For valid positions, compute in chunks of 512:
import torch.nn.functional as F
h = model.log2feats(seq)[pos.ne(0)]
y = pos[pos.ne(0)]
n = neg[pos.ne(0)]
a = (h * model.item_emb(y)).sum(-1, keepdim=True)
b = torch.einsum('nd,nkd->nk', h, model.item_emb(n))
logits = torch.cat([a, b], dim=1)
labels = torch.zeros(h.size(0), dtype=torch.long, device=h.device)
loss = F.cross_entropy(logits, labels)

Uniform sampling makes a common log-proposal correction cancel across these candidate columns. Do not introduce popularity sampling into this experiment without separately deriving its correction. Accumulate chunk gradients normalized by the batch's total valid-position count and perform one optimizer update per batch. At inference, use the original raw embedding dot products; no candidate softmax is required for ranking. Keep checkpoint and predictor metadata consistent with the unchanged GRU architecture.

directions.description: Change the negative proposal to a tempered training-frequency distribution, targeting more informative negatives while retaining broad coverage. Frequency-powered sampling is implemented in the authors' [official sampler](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/blob/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py) and described in the [original repository](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec).
directions.implementation:
Apply the common requirements in direction 1. Isolate the sampling change: retain baseline single-negative BPR, architecture, optimizer and hyperparameters. Compute counts exclusively from each category's training histories. Use an adaptation with a uniform floor:
counts = np.zeros(itemnum + 1, dtype=np.float64)
for history in user_train.values():
    np.add.at(counts, np.asarray(history, dtype=np.int64), 1)
weights = counts[1:] ** 0.5
if weights.sum() == 0:
    weights[:] = 1
q = 0.5 / itemnum + 0.5 * weights / weights.sum()
cdf = np.cumsum(q)
cdf[-1] = 1.0

def draw_negative(interacted):
    if len(interacted) >= itemnum:
        raise RuntimeError('No unobserved item available for negative sampling')
    while True:
        item = int(np.searchsorted(cdf, np.random.random(), side='right')) + 1
        if item not in interacted:
            return item

Replace only random.randint-based training-negative draws with draw_negative(interacted). Cache the CDF once per category rather than rebuilding it inside sample_batch. Keep its existing [B,T] negative return shape and family-specific diagnostic interface. Use the original BPR objective with a numerically stable equivalent:
losses = torch.nn.functional.softplus(neg_scores - pos_scores)
loss = losses[pos.ne(0)].mean()

The frequency table is a training sampler only. Do not save or use a separate popularity scorer in predict.py; prediction continues to load exactly one GRU checkpoint/category.

directions.description: Add independent dropout on GRU output features to regularize the scoring representation. The baseline currently drops input embeddings only; the authors' [official model](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/blob/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py) exposes separate embedding and hidden dropout.
